﴿God of mankind﴾ is likewise an explicative apposition, like the one before it, to show that to His lordship and His sovereignty has been added worship, which is founded on divinity, which requires complete power to dispose of everything fully, by bringing into existence and by annihilation. From this is His saying: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 31]. So He made clear that He is the King of mankind.

Then, a king may be a god and may not be a god. So He made clear that He is God, because the name "God" belongs to Him alone; no one shares it with Him. Also, He began with the name "Lord," which is the name of the one who has charge of a person's management and reform from the beginning of his life until he becomes a complete intelligent being. At that point, he knows by proof that he is a created slave, so he mentions that He is the King of mankind.

Then, when he knows that worship is binding upon him and obligatory for him, and that he is a created slave, and that his Creator is a worshipped God, glory be to Him makes clear that He is the God of mankind. He repeated the word "mankind" in the three places, because explicative apposition needs the distinction of clarification, and because repetition implies additional honor for mankind.

﴿From the evil of the whisperer﴾. Al-Farra' said: it is with a fatha on the waw, meaning as a noun: i.e., the one who whispers. With a kasra, it is the verbal noun: i.e., the whispering, like *al-zilzal* meaning *al-zalzala* (the earthquake). It was also said that with the fatha it is a noun meaning the whispering. The whispering is the speech of the soul, as one says: "his soul whispered to him a whispering," i.e., it spoke to him a speech. Its origin is a faint sound, and from this it is said that the sounds of ornaments are *waswas*. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

Al-Zajjaj said: the *waswas* is the devil, i.e., the one with the whispering. It is said that the *waswas* is a son of Iblis. The reality of the meaning of whispering has already been established in the explanation of His saying: ﴿Then Satan whispered to them both﴾ [al-A'raf: 20].

Written by Yahya ibn 'Ali al-Shawkani, may Allah forgive both of them.

The disagreement over whether it is Meccan or Medinan is like the disagreement that preceded it in the surah of al-Falaq.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾ was revealed in Mecca."

Ibn Mardawayh also transmitted from Ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾ was revealed in Medina." We have already mentioned in the surah of al-Falaq what was reported about the occasion of revelation of this surah and what was reported about its virtue, so refer back to it.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

The majority of reciters read ﴿qul a'udhu﴾ with the hamza (the glottal stop, *hamza*).

It was also read without it, with its vowel transferred to the lam.

The majority read ﴿an-nas﴾ without imala (the vowel-raising, *imala*, which pulls the final vowel toward i), while al-Kisa'i read it with imala.

The meaning of ﴿Lord of mankind﴾ is the one who owns their affairs and sets right their conditions. He said "Lord of mankind," although He is the Lord of all His creatures, to indicate their nobility, and because the seeking of refuge occurs from the evil of that which whispers in their breasts.

His saying ﴿King of mankind﴾ is an explicative apposition (*'atf al-bayan*, a kind of apposition that clarifies the word before it) brought to show that His lordship, glory be to Him, is not like the lordship of other kings over those under their hands of their slaves, but is by way of complete sovereignty and overpowering dominion.

﴿God of mankind﴾ is likewise an explicative apposition, like the one before it, to show that to His lordship and His sovereignty has been added worship, which is founded on divinity, which requires complete power to dispose of everything fully, by bringing into existence and by annihilation. Also, a lord may be a king and may not be a king, as one says "lord of the house" and "lord of the goods." From this is His saying: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 31]. So He made clear that He is the King of mankind.

Then, a king may be a god and may not be a god. So He made clear that He is God, because the name "God" belongs to Him alone; no one shares it with Him. Also, He began with the name "Lord," which is the name of the one who has charge of a person's management and reform from the beginning of his life until he becomes a complete intelligent being. At that point, he knows by proof that he is a created slave, so he mentions that He is the King of mankind.

Then, when he knows that worship is binding upon him and obligatory for him, and that he is a created slave, and that his Creator is a worshipped God, glory be to Him makes clear that He is the God of mankind. He repeated the word "mankind" in the three places, because explicative apposition needs the distinction of clarification, and because repetition implies additional honor for mankind.

﴿From the evil of the whisperer﴾. Al-Farra' said: it is with a fatha on the waw, meaning as a noun: i.e., the one who whispers. With a kasra, it is the verbal noun: i.e., the whispering, like *al-zilzal* meaning *al-zalzala* (the earthquake). It was also said that with the fatha it is a noun meaning the whispering. The whispering is the speech of the soul, as one says: "his soul whispered to him a whispering," i.e., it spoke to him a speech. Its origin is a faint sound, and from this it is said that the sounds of ornaments are *waswas*. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

*You hear for the ornaments a whispering when she turns away.*

Al-Zajjaj said: the *waswas* is the devil, i.e., the one with the whispering. It is said that the *waswas* is a son of Iblis. The reality of the meaning of whispering has already been established in the explanation of His saying: ﴿Then Satan whispered to them both﴾ [al-A'raf: 20].

The meaning of *al-khannas* is one who often withdraws, and it means holding back. One says "khanasa yakhnisu" when he withdraws. From this is the saying of al-'Ala' ibn al-Hadrami, praising the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

*When they treat with harm, forgive out of generosity, and if they fall silent at speech, do not ask.*

Mujahid said: when Allah is mentioned, he withdraws and shrinks back; and when He is not mentioned, he spreads out over the heart.

He is described as *al-khannas* because he often hides, and from this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So I swear by the stars that withdraw﴾ [al-Takwir: 15], meaning the stars, because they hide after appearing, as has already been mentioned. It was also said that *al-khannas* is a name for the son of Iblis, as was mentioned under *al-waswas*.

﴿Who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾. The relative pronoun may be in the position of a genitive as a qualifier of *al-waswas*; it may be in the accusative as a dispraise; and it may be in the nominative, by supposing an implied subject.

The meaning of whispering has already been mentioned.

Qatada said: the devil has a snout like a dog's snout in the chest of the human being. When the son of Adam is heedless of the remembrance of Allah, he whispers to him; and when the servant remembers his Lord, he withdraws.

Muqatil said: the devil is in the form of a pig, flowing through the son of Adam the way blood flows in his veins; Allah has empowered him over that. His whispering is calling to obedience to him with a hidden speech that reaches the heart without hearing any sound.

Then He, glory be to Him, made clear that the one who whispers is of two kinds: jinn and human. He said: ﴿From among the jinn and mankind﴾. As for the devil of the jinn, he whispers in the breasts of mankind. As for the devil of mankind, his whispering in the breasts of mankind is that he sees himself as a sincere, compassionate advisor, so he places in the breast, through his speech that he puts in the form of advice, what the devil places through his whispering. As He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Devils of mankind and jinn﴾ [al-An'am: 112]. It is also permissible for it to be connected to *yuwaswisu* (whispers), meaning: he whispers in their breasts from the direction of the jinn and from the direction of mankind. It is also permissible for it to be an explanation of *al-nas* (mankind).

Al-Razi said, and a group said: "from the jinn and mankind" are two categories subsumed under His saying ﴿in the breasts of mankind﴾, because the common quality between jinn and humans is called *insan* (human), and the human being is also called *insan*, so the word *insan* applies to the genus and the species by shared usage.

The evidence that the word *insan* includes the words *ins* (humans) and *jinn* is what is reported: a group of jinn came, and it was said to them: "Who are you?" They said: "People (*nas*) from the jinn."

Also, Allah called them men in His saying: ﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn﴾ [al-Jinn: 6]. It was also said that the meaning may be: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind from the whispering, the withdrawing one, who whispers in the breasts of mankind, and from the jinn and mankind, as if he sought refuge with his Lord from that one devil, then sought refuge with his Lord from all of the jinn and mankind. It was also said that the meaning of *al-nas* is *al-nasi* (the forgetful), and the *ya'* was dropped, as it is dropped in His saying: ﴿The day the caller calls﴾ [al-Qamar: 6]. Then He explained it with "jinn and mankind," because each individual of the two groups is generally afflicted with forgetfulness.

Better than this is that His saying "and mankind" is coordinated with *al-waswas*, meaning: from the evil of the whisperer and from the evil of mankind, as if he was commanded to seek refuge from the evil of jinn and humans.

Al-Hasan said: as for the devil of the jinn, he whispers in the breasts of mankind; as for the devil of mankind, he comes openly.

Qatada said: among the jinn there are devils, and among mankind there are devils. So we seek refuge in Allah from the devils of jinn and mankind.

It was also said that Iblis whispers in the breasts of the jinn as he whispers in the breasts of mankind, and the singular of *al-jinna* is *jinni*, just as the singular of *al-ins* is *insi*.

The first view is the strongest of these views, although the whispering of mankind in the breasts of mankind is only in the sense we mentioned earlier. This explanation serves as a reminder of the two weighty ones (jinn and mankind), to guide to the fact that whoever seeks refuge in Allah from both of them, the trials of this world and the Hereafter are removed from him.

Ibn Abi Dawud transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿the whisperer, the withdrawer﴾, that he said: The likeness of the devil is like that of the weasel (*ibn 'urs*), placing its mouth over the mouth of the heart, whispering to it. If he remembers Allah, he withdraws; and if he is silent, he returns to it. That is the whisperer, the withdrawer.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *Makayid al-Shaytan*, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Shahin, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab* transmitted from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed the devil has his snout placed on the heart of the son of Adam. If he remembers Allah, he withdraws; and if he forgets Him, he swallows the heart. That is the whisperer, the withdrawer."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿the whisperer, the withdrawer﴾, that he said: The devil crouches on the heart of the son of Adam. When he becomes forgetful and heedless, he whispers; and when he remembers Allah, he withdraws.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Diya' in *al-Mukhtara*, and al-Bayhaqi transmitted from him that he said: "No child is born except that the whisperer is upon its heart. When it remembers Allah, it withdraws; and when it is heedless, it whispers. That is His saying: ﴿the whisperer, the withdrawer﴾." Other than this has been reported in the meaning of this, and its apparent meaning is that the mere remembrance of Allah repels the devil, even if it is not by way of seeking refuge. Remembrance of Allah, glory be to Him, has great benefits, the essence of which is success in the good of this world and the Hereafter.

Here this blessed tafsir ends, by the pen of its author Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Shawkani, may Allah forgive his sins.
